name: Extended water fasting

lead: An extended water fast means eating nothing and drinking only water for several days. People use 2 to 7 day fasts to drop scale weight quickly and look leaner and less bloated before starting a cut or lean bulk.

The body first makes glucose from protein and stores, then shifts to ketosis and runs on ketones. Medical literature describes about 0.9 kg lost per day in the first week, with much of the early loss coming from water and lean tissue. Appearance outcomes have not been studied.

paras: Users typically run a fast of a few days, drinking water (often with added electrolytes) and nothing else, then ease back onto food and move into a cut or lean bulk. The scale drop shows within days; how much of it is fat versus water and lean tissue varies.

Documented risks include electrolyte imbalance, gallstones and refeeding syndrome after roughly 4 to 5 days or more without food, which can be potentially fatal. Minerals such as sodium and potassium fall during the fast. People with medical conditions, and anyone prone to disordered eating, are generally advised to avoid it.

angle.text: A multi-day water-only fast produces a rapid scale-weight drop that people use to look leaner and less bloated before a cut or lean bulk. Research on prolonged fasts shows early loss that includes water and lean tissue, and appearance outcomes have not been studied.

lead: Extended or prolonged water fasting means consuming no food, only water, for more than 24 hours, typically five to twenty days in the literature.[1] In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed for rapid fat loss before a cut or lean bulk, and for 2 to 7 day attempts.[2][3]

Medical literature describes weight loss of about 0.9 kg per day in the first week, much of it early on from lean tissue and water, and documents risks including refeeding syndrome, electrolyte imbalance and gallstones.[1]

paras: Early in a fast the body relies on gluconeogenesis, and later shifts into ketosis in which ketones replace glucose as the main fuel for the central nervous system.[1] Sodium, potassium and magnesium drop markedly and can lead to hyponatremia.[1]

Average loss is about 0.9 kg per day in the first week and about 0.3 kg per day by the third week.[1] During the early gluconeogenic phase roughly two-thirds of weight lost is lean muscle; afterward the ratio of fat to lean tissue lost is roughly 7:6.[1]

Wikipedia cites a 2024 narrative review on the efficacy and safety of prolonged water fasting.[1] No controlled trials of extended water fasting for facial or physical appearance were found, and Wikipedia reports no sound clinical evidence that fasting extends human longevity.[1]

Reintroducing too much food after roughly 4 to 5 days or more without eating can cause refeeding syndrome, with low potassium, magnesium and phosphate and potentially fatal complications.[1] Fasting also raises gallstone risk through reduced gallbladder motility and cholesterol-saturated bile during rapid weight loss.[1] In 1932 physician Morris Fishbein stated that prolonged fasting is never necessary and invariably does harm, presented as historical commentary.[1]

Posters ask whether to start a cut with a 2 to 3 day water fast; some replies predict binge eating afterward and suggest a modest daily deficit instead.[3] Another thread, started as a joke, features a poster planning a seven-day fast while weight training and replies saying he would not last.[4] Threads also ask about water fasting while on semaglutide.[2]

lore.intro: Water fasting appears in forums as a fast route to a leaner face, often debated against a steady deficit.[3][4]

claims.claim: A multi-day water fast removes fat faster than a calorie deficit.

timeline.event: Angus Barbieri begins a 382-day medically monitored fast, ending June 1966.[1]
